title: Sine equals cosine of the complement
subtitle: Right triangles and trigonometry · 7 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **7 of the official questions in Right triangles and trigonometry are this one** — 0 Easy, 2 Medium, 5 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You see sine of one angle set equal to cosine of another angle, or the problem says two angles add to 90 degrees (or π/2 radians), with no side lengths anywhere.
- The angle measures are often algebraic expressions in x, or the answer choices are trig expressions of different angles.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Use sin(A) = cos(B) exactly when A + B = 90° (π/2 in radians).
- 2) If the angles are expressions, set their sum equal to 90 and solve the linear equation.
- If the question asks for a trig value, swap sin for cos of the complementary angle and copy the value across.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Helps only when the angles are expressions: type (first angle expression) + (second angle expression) = 90 and read the x-intercept, or graph both sides and find where they cross.
For value-swap questions it adds nothing, because the answer is the same number with no calculation needed.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You set the two angle expressions equal to each other instead of making them add to 90, or you give the value for the wrong function (sin instead of cos, or the reciprocal ratio).
Radian versions catch you if you use 90 instead of π/2.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
